output.name: Tirun

anatomy.part: stern tip of the upturned hull, where the planks meet the water on the left
rear planks, on the inner plank line just below the arch on the stern side
crown of the keel, the highest point of the upturned dome
bow rim, where the curve of the hull turns down to the water on the right
midships, on the underside of the hull at the lower bow curve
bow foot, the lower tip of the stem where the lantern's tether is made fast
the lit lantern hanging beneath the keel, ringed

output.myth: Tirun came home keel-up in the spring gale, with no crew aboard and her lamp still lit underneath. Hesk, who keeps count at the pole, went down the tally and found eleven names missing and no reel that had let them go. Tavo the Gale laughed when the old women asked him, and said he had only lifted the boat, not drowned anyone. Aun, who cut the string, would not say what he had seen. Ennu the Kite-Wright came with bone and cloth and turned the hull over to look. Under the planks there was a lamp, trimmed by someone careful, and nobody in the islands can say whose hands. So the boat sits up in Vel with its light under the keel. When the wind is wrong, the old ones say, you can see that light moving beneath it, like someone still bailing, still counting, still looking for the way home.
output.verse:
Keel-up in the dark,
a lamp still burns beneath her
no hands to bail her.
